🥘 Ingredients

  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 large carrot, diced
  • 1 celery stalk, diced
  • 1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes
  • 4 cups vegetable broth
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried basil
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • 6 lasagna noodles, broken into bite-sized pieces
  • 1 cup ricotta cheese
  • 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
  • Fresh basil leaves, for garnish

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrot, and celery, cooking gently until softened and fragrant, about 5-7 minutes. This step builds the flavor base by releasing the sweetness of the vegetables and softening them so they blend smoothly into the broth. Avoid rushing this part, as the gentle sauté enhances the soup’s depth and complexity.
  2. Add the minced garlic and cook for another 1-2 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent burning. Garlic releases its pungent flavor quickly, so it’s important to watch it carefully to avoid bitterness. Once fragrant and lightly golden, stir in the crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, oregano, and dried basil. Season with salt and pepper. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
  3. Once simmering, add the broken lasagna noodles to the pot. Stir to prevent sticking and cook until the noodles are tender but still hold their shape, about 10-12 minutes. Stir occasionally to ensure even cooking and prevent noodles from clumping. The noodles absorb the broth’s flavor and thicken the soup, so don’t overcook to avoid mushiness.
  4. Taste the soup and adjust seasoning with more salt or pepper if needed. Remove the pot from heat. Ladle the soup into bowls and spoon dollops of ricotta cheese on top. The ricotta adds a creamy, cooling contrast to the tangy tomato base. Finish with a sprinkle of grated Parmesan and fresh basil leaves for a bright, herbaceous note.
  5. Serve immediately while hot. The contrast of the warm broth with the creamy ricotta is what makes this soup so comforting and delicious. If you like, pair with crusty garlic bread for a complete meal.
  6. To reheat leftovers, warm gently on the stovetop over low heat, adding a splash of vegetable broth or water if the soup has thickened too much. Stir frequently to prevent sticking and maintain a smooth texture.
  7. If you want to prepare ahead, cook the soup through step 4 but hold off on adding the ricotta and fresh basil until serving. This keeps the cheese fresh and basil vibrant, preserving their texture and flavor.
  8. For a thicker soup, simmer uncovered for a few extra minutes after the noodles cook to reduce the broth slightly. This concentrates the flavors and creates a heartier texture.
  9. To make the soup spicier, add a pinch of crushed red pepper flakes when cooking the garlic. This adds a subtle heat that complements the tomato and herbs well without overpowering the dish.

  • 1 cup whole milk, room temperature
  • Orange and gold gel food coloring
  • Edible gold leaf for decoration
  • Buttercream frosting: 1 cup unsalted butter, softened; 4 cups powdered sugar; 2 tsp vanilla extract; 2-3 tbsp milk

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 9-inch round cake pans, then line them with parchment paper. Sifting the flour, baking powder, and salt together ensures the dry ingredients are evenly mixed and free of lumps, which helps the cake rise evenly and stay tender. Mixing dry ingredients separately before combining with wet prevents overmixing, which can make the cake dense. Be gentle when folding the flour into the wet ingredients to keep the batter light.
  2. In a large bowl, cream the softened butter and granulated sugar together until light and fluffy, about 4-5 minutes. This step incorporates air into the batter, which is crucial for a tender crumb. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition to prevent curdling. Stir in vanilla extract. Alternate adding the dry ingredients and milk in three parts, beginning and ending with the dry. Mix just until combined to avoid toughening the cake.
  3. Divide the batter evenly between the two prepared pans. Tap the pans gently on the counter to release any large air bubbles. Bake in the preheated oven for 28-32 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Avoid opening the oven door too early to prevent the cake from sinking.
  4. Allow the cakes to cool in their pans for 10 minutes, then turn them out onto wire racks to cool completely. Cooling the cakes fully before frosting is essential to prevent the buttercream from melting and sliding off.
  5. Prepare the buttercream by beating softened butter until creamy. Gradually add powdered sugar, beating on low speed to avoid a sugar cloud, then increase speed to medium-high until fluffy. Add vanilla and milk one tablespoon at a time to reach desired consistency. Tint the buttercream with orange gel food coloring until you achieve a soft pastel shade.
  6. Level the cooled cakes with a serrated knife to create flat surfaces for stacking. Place one cake layer on your serving plate or cake board. Spread a generous layer of the orange-tinted buttercream over the top, smoothing it evenly. This layering adds moisture and color contrast inside the cake.
  7. Place the second cake layer on top and apply a thin crumb coat of buttercream over the entire cake to seal in crumbs. Chill the cake in the fridge for 15-20 minutes to set the crumb coat before applying the final thick layer of frosting. This step ensures a smooth finish.
  8. Apply the final thick layer of buttercream, smoothing with an offset spatula. Use a small spatula or brush to add edible gold leaf accents in the shape of the Leo zodiac symbol and scatter edible glitter or small stars on top for sparkle. The gold leaf adds a luxurious touch that catches the light beautifully.
  9. Allow the cake to rest in the fridge for at least 30 minutes before serving to let the frosting set fully. Bring to room temperature about 20 minutes before slicing for the best texture and flavor. This resting time helps the flavors meld and the cake slice cleanly.

  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, and ginger. Mixing the dry ingredients well ensures the spices are evenly distributed, so every bite has balanced flavor. If you rush this step, you might get uneven pockets of spice or leavening that affect texture.
  3. In a separate bowl, combine the pumpkin puree, granulated sugar, brown sugar, vegetable oil, eggs, vanilla extract, and milk. Whisk until smooth and fully blended. This wet mixture provides moisture and richness, while the sugars add sweetness and help caramelize the crust. The milk adds tenderness to the crumb.

Then pour the remaining batter on top and finish with the rest of the cinnamon sugar. This layering creates the signature cinnamon swirl that caramelizes during baking for that irresistible texture and flavor contrast.
  6. Using a butter knife or skewer, gently swirl the batter and cinnamon sugar layers together in an S or figure-eight pattern. This step creates the beautiful marbled effect without blending the cinnamon sugar completely into the batter. The swirl should be visible but not overmixed.
  7. Bake the pumpkin bread in the preheated oven for 50 to 60 minutes. Start checking at 50 minutes by inserting a toothpick into the center. It should come out mostly clean with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter. Baking too long will dry it out, too short and it will be undercooked and dense.
  8. Let the bread cool in the pan on a wire rack for 15 minutes before removing it. Cooling slightly allows the bread to set and makes it easier to slice without crumbling. Removing it too soon can cause it to break apart, while waiting too long can make slicing harder.
  9. Once cooled, slice the pumpkin bread with a serrated knife for clean cuts. Serve warm with butter or cream cheese if desired.   • Assorted sprinkles for decorating
  • 24 lollipop sticks

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by crumbling your cooled vanilla cake into a large mixing bowl. Use your hands or a fork to break it down into fine crumbs without large chunks. This step is important because uniform crumbs will mix better with the frosting, creating a consistent texture for your cake pops.
  2. Add the cream cheese frosting to the cake crumbs a little at a time, mixing gently with a spoon or your hands. You want just enough frosting to bind the crumbs together so they hold their shape when rolled into balls, but not so much that the mixture becomes sticky or soggy. This balance ensures the cake pops stay moist but firm.
  3. Roll the cake mixture into 1-inch balls, placing them on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Try to keep the balls uniform in size for even coating and presentation. Once rolled, chill the balls in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to firm up. This step is crucial because chilled cake balls dip more easily and hold their shape better.
  4. Prepare your melted white chocolate or candy melts in a microwave-safe bowl. Heat in 30-second intervals, stirring in between, until smooth and fully melted. Be careful not to overheat, as chocolate can seize and become grainy. Smooth chocolate ensures an even coating on your cake pops.
  5. Dip the tip of each lollipop stick into the melted chocolate, then insert it about halfway into a chilled cake ball. This 'glue' helps secure the stick inside the cake pop so it won’t fall out during dipping or handling.
  6. Dip each cake pop into the melted chocolate, fully coating it. Gently tap off excess chocolate by tapping the stick on the bowl edge. This technique prevents thick, uneven coatings and helps the chocolate set smoothly.
  7. Immediately decorate the dipped cake pops with sprinkles before the chocolate sets. Working quickly is key because once the coating hardens, sprinkles won’t stick well.
  8. Place the decorated cake pops upright in a styrofoam block or a cake pop stand to dry completely. Let them sit at room temperature or in the refrigerator until the chocolate coating is fully set, about 15-20 minutes.
